record.original_question: Does the collection of known polynomial invariants of degree at most 9 cut out the algebraic variety of 4×4×4 contingency tables (pijk) over C that have tensor rank at most 4, equivalently tables admitting a decomposition pijk = ρAi·σAj·θAk + ρCi·σCj·θCk + ρGi·σGj·θGk + ρTi·σTj·θTk for i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}?

evidence.quote: Specific Problem: Consider the variety of 4×4×4-tables of tensor rank at most 4. There are certain known polynomials of degree at most nine which vanish on this variety. Do they suffice to cut out the variety?

The model referred to in the Specific Problem lives in the 64-dimensional space C^4 ⊗ C^4 ⊗ C^4 of 4×4×4-tables (pijk), where i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}. It has the parametric representation pijk = ρAi · σAj · θAk + ρCi · σCj · θCk + ρGi · σGj · θGk + ρTi · σTj · θTk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex numbers. Let $I=\{A,C,G,T\}$ and consider the 64-dimensional space $\mathbb{C}^4\otimes\mathbb{C}^4\otimes\mathbb{C}^4$ of $4\times 4\times 4$ tables $(p_{ijk})_{i,j,k\in I}$. Define the variety $X\subset\mathbb{C}^{4\times 4\times 4}$ to be the Zariski closure of the set of tensors of tensor rank at most $4$, i.e. tables admitting a decomposition
$$p_{ijk}=\rho^A_i\sigma^A_j\theta^A_k+\rho^C_i\sigma^C_j\theta^C_k+\rho^G_i\sigma^G_j\theta^G_k+\rho^T_i\sigma^T_j\theta^T_k$$
for vectors $\rho^a,\sigma^a,\theta^a\in\mathbb{C}^4$, $a\in I$. Three families of homogeneous polynomials are known to vanish on $X$:
(i) the degree-$5$ "Strassen commutativity" polynomials,
(ii) the degree-$6$ Landsberg–Manivel polynomials, and
(iii) certain degree-$9$ symmetrization polynomials.
Question: Do these known polynomials of degree at most $9$ cut out $X$ set-theoretically; that is, is $X$ equal to the common zero locus in $\mathbb{C}^{4\times 4\times 4}$ of these polynomials?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the set-theoretic version of Allman's "salmon conjecture" for the fourth secant variety of the Segre embedding of $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^3$. It was approached computationally by Bates and Oeding ("Toward a Salmon Conjecture", 2011) and then proved (without numerical computation) by Friedland and Gross, "A proof of the set-theoretic version of the salmon conjecture" (J. Algebra, 2012; arXiv:1104.1776). The stronger ideal-theoretic version remains open.

status_evidence.title: A proof of the set-theoretic version of the salmon conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Friedland and Gross show that the irreducible variety of 4x4x4 complex tensors of border rank at most 4 is the zero set of polynomial equations of degree 5, 6, and 9.
status_evidence.claim: The set-theoretic salmon conjecture for 4x4x4 tensors of border rank ≤4 is proved.

status_evidence.title: Toward a Salmon Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Bates and Oeding provide numerical evidence and a computational approach toward the salmon conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier computational work toward resolving the set-theoretic version.
